## Strategy guide

### Strategic thesis

Saar’s kit makes early expansion, movement, income, and production unusually easy. Manage the attention that advantage attracts: use mobile factories and infantry to build a flexible position, but avoid becoming the only credible leader. A large early board is leverage, yet it gives the table time to coordinate against you. Preserve late scoring options, including after losing your home planets. The guide’s recurring advice is to play tightly enough to remain a late-game threat rather than an obvious early leader. [C01, C02, C24]

This January 2024 SCPT guide is ASR-transcribed; later rules compatibility is unreviewed. “Mellon,” “Lysus,” and “Zobat” may be planet-name recognition errors. [C25]

### Opening choices and round one

**Default: take Construction when the pick is uncertain or you want a robust opening.** Saar’s floating factories are valuable and vulnerable to Reactor Meltdown, so a second dock both protects against losing the only one and unlocks the commander once three are on the board. It also gives flexibility to develop in more than one direction instead of sending every ship and build toward one threatening front. The guide frames Construction as insurance and a relatively low-escalation choice; it is especially attractive for a newer Saar player. It is not an absolute rule: Warfare is the major exception when Saar can exploit its unusually large movement and expansion ceiling. [C03, C04]

Construction can be played early because Saar does not need to land on a planet first just to move its home dock away; however, placing a dock still requires a planet in the system. If a structure objective or forward PDS qualification is at issue, timing and the objective may make taking a planet before the card more useful. Construction’s secondary still builds on planets, and Warfare’s secondary can use only one space dock in a system. These are easy details to mishandle when Saar has multiple mobile docks. [C05]

**Warfare is a high-ceiling alternative when expansion or custodians timing is decisive.** Moving the starting forces forward, lifting the token, and then spreading out can take several planet systems and potentially set up an easy Mecatol Rex approach. One suggested line is to establish the forward position, then use Warfare to clear the home-system token and move out again. Depending on slice and timing, this can produce a very large round-one footprint. But it brings the cost with it: Saar’s wealth and reach make it easy to draw immediate hostility, and a second-action Warfare play can disrupt neighbors’ expected technology or production timing. Choose this line when you can tolerate the political response and have a plan for what those systems do for your scoring pace. [C06, C07]

Leadership is a sound, medium-strength pick when you want command-token momentum and room to follow Technology, Warfare, or Construction. Saar starts with extra carriers and can activate several systems, so it can burn tokens fast; Fleet Pool can constrain later movement. Diplomacy offers resources and can enable custodians, but the hosts describe it as a less attractive route than Saar’s other options. Politics can preserve money for a later Mecatol attempt, but delays the point and risks another player taking it. Trade combines money for technology/plastic with goodwill; it is a lower-drama custodians route than Warfare. [C08, C09, C10]

Do not take Technology just because Saar can afford it. The agent already helps movement, Scavenge adds money as Saar expands, and plastic often creates more reach and threat than an extra technology. The guide’s rule of thumb is that Chaos Mapping is the essential faction technology; Gravity Drive is an opening-specific choice, and Carrier II is a strong follow-up. If Gravity Drive is what makes round-one custodians possible, prioritize it. Otherwise, Chaos Mapping first can support a slower game, followed by Carrier II for capacity and a deeper fighter screen. The speakers disagree in emphasis about how much Gravity Drive improves the game, but agree it is not mandatory in every position. [C11, C12]

### Economy, production, and force composition

Scavenge pays one trade good after Saar gains control of a planet. The mech can then be deployed by spending a trade good after that same gain, so the income can effectively fund a mech when you value the mech more than keeping the money. On an explored planet, exploration happens before the control trigger, so this timing does not let Saar spend a newly gained trade good to influence that exploration. Early expansion therefore funds both builds and selective mech deployment, but the trade good remains a real opportunity cost. [C13]

Chaos Mapping is powerful because it allows a unit to be produced at the start of each of Saar’s turns in a system with one of its units that has Production. It accelerates plastic without requiring a normal tactical build action, so the earlier Saar researches it, the more turns it can pay off. Do not treat this as a full production build or assume Sarween Tools applies: the guide stresses the wording distinction between “produce” and the Production ability. The start-of-turn unit also does not make Saar a stall faction; it tends to spend actions quickly. [C14]

The floating factories are mobile production and capacity platforms, but a high printed production value is only useful when Saar can pay for the units and move them where needed. The guide recommends prioritizing plastic over optional technologies, especially once Chaos Mapping is online. Carrier II adds capacity that can turn a captured system into a defensible one by adding fighters; Saar’s docks also contribute capacity. An infantry-first opening is a useful alternative to filling carriers with fighters immediately: infantry secures planets and does not consume ship capacity, while early opponents often lack the ground forces to dislodge it. Later, pivot into fighters once Carrier II and the board position support them. This plan is conditional on not leaving critical space fleets undefended. [C15, C16]

Floating Factory II can be worthwhile if Saar reaches it without delaying more urgent movement, production, or scoring needs. It improves the dock’s movement and production/capacity, but the two-yellow route is costly and the speakers say it often arrives late (around round four). Consider it when a rich game, technology objective, or existing yellow access makes the investment reasonable. Commander-enabled production routing still obeys production capacity and cannot send units to a dock that is blockaded. [C17]

### Mobility and tactical positioning

Saar’s agent, Captain Mendosa (ASR spelling; reference lists “Mendosa”), can raise one activated ship’s move value to match the highest move value on the board. The speakers note Saar’s own cruiser gives a round-one move-two option for a carrier or factory, before other movement modifiers apply. Gravity Drive can then add movement, which can make an early Mecatol grab possible. Treat the agent as an important option with an opportunity cost: using it for your own move is often valuable, but the guide says it can be sold when custodians are out of reach and a buyer’s deal is better. Terrain and modifiers still matter; the source’s nebula discussion is an example of why “move value” is not the same as total movement. [C18]

Chaos Mapping also protects Saar ships in asteroid fields from opponents activating those systems, helping Saar hold a mobile production and movement network. The guide warns that this is not blanket immunity: effects that move ships without activation, including the cited Benediction interaction, can pull a fleet out of safety. Do not pass while your only viable retreat or survival position depends on the asteroid field. Losing access at the wrong moment can make an otherwise threatening Saar position vulnerable to a coordinated attack. [C19, C20]

Dark Energy Tap is a flexible later option when the economy supports it. Frontier exploration can provide tokens or money, and retreat can help a mobile faction whose fleet has moved away from its controlled planets. The retreat option is especially useful when Saar has several ground-force positions or empty systems to retreat toward. Avoid a position where a retreat would strand one floating factory on another and lock both into a bad position. DET competes with more immediate technology or plastic, so take it when its exploration and escape routes solve a real late-game problem. [C21]

### Scoring and endgame

Saar can score objectives without controlling its home-system planets. That weakens the common win-slay line of taking home to prevent scoring and gives Saar a way to keep scoring after losing the home planets. It does not make Saar impossible to eliminate: Saar still needs planets for placing floating factories through Construction and can be defeated through other routes. Keep planets and infantry distributed enough to avoid being eliminated, and do not mistake home-system scoring protection for general safety. [C02, C05]

The hosts describe Saar as broadly capable of stage-one, secret, and stage-two scoring, with exceptions. Saar can pursue custodians, take Mecatol later with Imperial, and produce units when a unit-based secret requires them. A nine-ground-force secret is easier when Saar builds infantry onto a controlled planet while its dock remains in the system. These are preparation advantages, not automatic points: check the objective requirements and timing. [C22]

“Improve Infrastructure” is a notable bad fit because Saar’s floating factory is in space and does not count as a structure on a planet; the source says PDS is the relevant structure for that objective. Whether to invest in PDS depends on the revealed objectives, Saar’s path to ten, and whether the point can be replaced by a stage two, bonus point, or Imperial/Mecatol point. Do not sink resources into PDS by default. A PDS secret can change the calculation, while Dark Energy Tap can help cycle secrets if Saar needs another draw. [C23]

The hero can destroy other players’ infantry and fighters in a system adjacent to one of Saar’s space docks. The guide presents it as a late-game answer to a high-HP fleet that Saar might otherwise struggle to clear. “Adjacent” means an adjacent system, not units in the same system as the dock; the hero does not clear ground forces directly below a dock. Preserve the hero until a strategically important system and the relevant enemy units line up. [C24]

### Politics, deals, and counters

Saar begins with threat heat; acknowledge it openly. Scavenge income and mobile docks let Saar offer friendly planet trades, pay for goodwill, and use the promissory note to preserve ground forces. Rog’s Call is often more useful to Saar than to the recipient: it relocates Saar’s ground forces after an opponent commits to land, letting Saar avoid combat and redeploy those forces. The guide notes the recipient chooses where those forces go, so do not promise a destination you cannot control. [C25]

Extortion should be a credible choice, not a bluff made on the assumption that the other player will yield. Before demanding a Support for the Throne or payment, decide whether following through benefits Saar even if it creates a lasting enemy. A small payment to redirect Saar toward another threat, or a support swap that removes Saar from someone’s immediate concern, may be more reliable than making yourself the whole table’s target. Table culture matters: a group comfortable with aggression may accept a sharper threat; another table may coordinate to slow Saar down. [C26]

Against Saar, opponents should respect its mobility, income, and capacity to put pressure on home systems early, while avoiding trades that strengthen an already leading Saar player. Do not assume taking both Saar home planets is always a punishment: the source points out that this can remove Saar’s own contingency for Shard of the Throne scoring. If contesting Saar’s home, leaving one planet may preserve a way to deny that point later. Chaos Mapping’s asteroid protection can be bypassed by non-activation movement effects, so watch for those effects and time a strike when Saar leaves safety or has passed. Saar players should likewise avoid spreading so far that the entire table can coordinate against the only obvious leader. [C20, C27]

## Combined source guidance

The guide above contains conditional, transcript-cited advice. The pinned documents below add community research and a bot-oriented mid/late-game profile. Their ordered technology/build lists are proposals, not unconditional policy targets. Keep source disagreements and expansion assumptions visible.

**Historical scope:** upstream statements about available factions, engine support, bot behavior and benchmark results describe that source revision; they are not checks of this checkout. Podcast timestamps in upstream notes are approximate and do not share the local transcript verification.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The Clan of Saar (`saar`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-clan-of-saar-saar) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-clan-of-saar-saar)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home Ragh 2/1 and Lisis II 1/0; start 2 carriers, 1 cruiser, 2 fighters, 4
infantry, Floating Factory (move 1, capacity 4, PRODUCTION 5, in space, destroyed if blockaded);
starting tech Antimass Deflectors. Scavenge: a trade good each time it gains a planet. Nomadic:
can score without controlling its home planets. Faction techs Chaos Mapping (B: asteroid fields
with Saar ships cannot be activated; produce 1 unit at the start of each turn) and Floating Factory
II (YY). Agent: raise one ship's move to the board's fastest. Commander (3 docks): fighters and
infantry may be placed at any dock. Mech deploys for 1 trade good after taking a planet.

**Opening.** Three capacity units at the start (two carriers and the dock) and Scavenge make Saar
the best round-1 expander; prioritise a slice with many two-planet systems and a road to Mecatol
Rex. One school takes Warfare and delays it while spreading 1 carrier + 2 infantry per system,
collecting a trade good per planet; another takes Technology (Gravity Drive and Sarween) then
Mecatol Rex in round 2 with the dock along
([BGG TomBoombs Saar guide, 2020](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2349874);
[BGG Saar speaker question, 2020](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2437176)).
Do not pop Construction first: wait for the Scavenge trade good to afford research.

**Technology.** Sarween Tools and Gravity Drive first (Gravity Drive moves the dock too), then
Carrier II and Dreadnought II; Floating Factory II is a luxury (mostly for the "both faction
technologies" secret). Disagreement on Chaos Mapping: "game-changing, makes Saar uneliminable" when
an asteroid field is reachable versus "situational"
([BGG "Saar Tech Path", 2021](https://boardgamegeek.com/thread/2620083)).

**Builds and play.** Move docks with the fleet and produce on arrival; never leave a dock without
escorts (blockade destroys it); retreat docks rather than lose them; a dock in an asteroid field
with Chaos Mapping is a permanent base. Keep trade goods low when Mentak can Pillage.

**Objectives.** Plan to reach the first stage II reveal with about 8 points (custodians, support,
secrets, stage I), uneliminable, 16 trade goods and three unit upgrades (TomBoombs). Saar struggle
with technology and structure-on-planet objectives
([r/ti 2025 tier list comments](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/1kylhx4/faction_power_tier_list/)).

**Diplomacy.** "The heat won't turn off": Saar draws hate whatever it does; extortion of neighbours
for support/ceasefire swaps is in the playbook. Ghosts placing wormholes in an empty Saar slice and
Mentak's Pillage are the named threats.

**Strength.** SCPT top row 2022 and S 2025; async PoK data only B ("overrated", "draws heat").

**Bot feasibility.**
- The engine already treats the Floating Factory as a non-ship for activation (comment in
  `activation_value`). Moving docks forward with escorts and producing on arrival needs a "dock
  follows fleet" movement rule. Value high, effort M.
- Opening: spread one carrier and two infantry per system (the bot's opening plan does this), and
  value each planet +1 for Scavenge in `planet_worth`. Value medium, effort S.
- Research: Sarween, Gravity Drive, Carrier II, Dreadnought II; Chaos Mapping when an asteroid
  field is adjacent to its systems. Effort S.
- Safety: never end a turn with a dock alone next to enemy ships. Effort M.
- Hard: the extortion game.

</details>

## Strategy connections

- [Scavenge](../components.md#ability-scavenge) **synergizes-with** [Scavenger Zeta](../components.md#unit-saar-mech). After gaining a planet, the Scavenge trade good can be spent for that planet’s mech; the trade good has an opportunity cost. Sources: [SCPT 336, 1402.18–1479.08s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm) **synergizes-with** [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock). Chaos Mapping’s start-of-turn production rewards Saar for having a Production unit in useful systems and for researching the technology early. Sources: [SCPT 336, 2076.10–2156.18s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm) **conflicts-with** [Sarween Tools](../components.md#technology-st). The guide distinguishes Chaos Mapping’s “produce” effect from the Production ability and says Sarween Tools does not discount this effect. Sources: [SCPT 336, 2223.04–2286.10s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm) **synergizes-with** [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd). Chaos Mapping is the guide’s continuing priority; Gravity Drive is a conditional first pick when it enables custodians or a necessary reach breakpoint. Sources: [SCPT 336, 3576.12–3649.00s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm) **enables** [Carrier II](../components.md#technology-cv2). The guide describes Chaos Mapping followed by Carrier II as a viable shallow technology route that adds capacity without requiring Gravity Drive in every game. Sources: [SCPT 336, 3711.90–3894.46s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Captain Mendosa](../components.md#leader-saaragent) **synergizes-with** [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd). The agent’s increased move value combines with Gravity Drive’s later modifier when a movement breakpoint such as custodians matters. Sources: [SCPT 336, 1740.62–1768.80s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction) **enables** [Floating Factory II](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock2). Construction provides Saar another dock, reducing single-dock vulnerability and progressing the three-dock commander unlock. Sources: [SCPT 336, 2786.66–2843.82s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock) **requires** [Rowl Sarring](../components.md#leader-saarcommander). The commander unlock requires three space docks on the board; routing produced infantry or fighters also requires an unblocked destination dock and remains within production capacity. Sources: [SCPT 336, 1815.76–1902.96s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm) **synergizes-with** [Dark Energy Tap](../components.md#technology-det). Chaos Mapping protects Saar’s asteroid-field presence while Dark Energy Tap can provide frontier access and alternative retreat destinations; DET is a later, economy-dependent investment. Sources: [SCPT 336, 2305.46–2348.06s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/); [SCPT 336, 4370.00–4492.20s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Gurno Aggero](../components.md#leader-saarhero) **counters** [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock). The hero destroys opposing infantry and fighters in a system adjacent to a Saar dock, offering a late-game answer to units that otherwise absorb Saar’s attacks. Sources: [SCPT 336, 1910.26–2004.54s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Improve Infrastructure](../components.md#public-objective-infrastructure) **conflicts-with** [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock). Improve Infrastructure counts structures on planets; a Saar floating factory is in space, so Saar may need PDS or an alternate scoring route. Sources: [SCPT 336, 5173.80–5224.34s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
- [Imperial](../components.md#strategy-card-pok8imperial) **scores** [The Clan of Saar](saar.md). The guide identifies taking Mecatol with Imperial later as a conditional scoring route when Saar needs the point and can meet the card and objective timing. Sources: [SCPT 336, 4545.02–4573.80s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** Play Saar tightly and conservatively: use its strong tempo without becoming the only obvious leader, since an overextended early lead gives the table time to coordinate and can make Saar eliminable.
  Conditions: Especially relevant in rounds four and five when the table can compare scoring pace and coordinate; adjust to table awareness and Saar’s actual survival position. Compatibility: SCPT faction guide published 2024-01-31; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Strategic opinion from guide hosts; tempo examples are not guaranteed outcomes.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 5432–5606s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [The Clan of Saar](saar.md)
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** Nomadic lets Saar score objectives without controlling its home-system planets, but Saar can still be eliminated and still needs planets to place floating factories through Construction.
  Conditions: Use the scoring protection when planning late scoring or resisting a home-system win-slay; maintain other planets and forces to avoid elimination. Compatibility: Guide discussion of Prophecy of Kings-era Saar; current rules not independently checked. Uncertainty: The guide explicitly distinguishes home scoring from elimination; exact elimination edge cases are not analyzed.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 1038–1071s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/) · [SCPT 336 1193–1221s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Nomadic](../components.md#ability-nomadic), [The Clan of Saar](saar.md), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock), [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Construction is a robust default when Saar wants a safe opening: a second mobile dock provides insurance against losing the first and lets Saar develop in more than one direction.
  Conditions: Particularly useful for a newer Saar player or when the table is likely to deny Construction later; Warfare is a major alternative when its expansion ceiling is worth the heat. Compatibility: Guide strategic recommendation; strategy card rules and table meta not separately verified. Uncertainty: Hosts call it an easy default but also explicitly discuss Warfare as an exception.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2481–2504s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/) · [SCPT 336 2752–2903s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock), [Floating Factory II](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock2), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** A second Saar space dock insures against Reactor Meltdown destroying the only dock; three docks also unlock Saar’s commander, whose alliance can be sold once available.
  Conditions: Prioritize early Construction when the first dock is exposed or commander access and an alliance sale will matter. Compatibility: Guide component discussion; current interaction details not independently reviewed. Uncertainty: The guide characterizes Reactor Meltdown risk as a reason for Construction; the actual threat depends on card access and table decisions.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2787–2844s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock), [Floating Factory II](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock2), [Rowl Sarring](../components.md#leader-saarcommander), [Alliance](../components.md#promissory-color-an)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Construction’s secondary requires a controlled planet to place a Saar space dock; Warfare’s secondary can build from only one dock in a system. Saar may pop Construction early without first landing if placing its dock is otherwise legal.
  Conditions: Check whether a planet is present and controlled before placing a dock, and whether one or multiple docks are in the activated system when following Warfare. Compatibility: Rule interpretation stated by SCPT in the 2024 guide; verify against the table’s governing rules if rules precision is essential. Uncertainty: Transcript contains a few jokes and broad shorthand; claim retains the specific caveats stated in the episode.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 1175–1260s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/) · [SCPT 336 2905–2931s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction), [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock)
<a id="claim-c06"></a>

- **Draft:** Warfare can turn Saar’s multiple starting carriers and mobile dock into a high-expansion round: move forces forward, lift the token, then spread to several systems or approach Mecatol Rex.
  Conditions: Best when slice geometry, action order, and available resources make the expansion useful for objectives or a custodians attempt. Compatibility: Guide’s opening advice; outcome depends on map, draft order, and opponents. Uncertainty: The hosts describe a high ceiling, not an automatic number of planets or custodians point.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 3070–3137s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock)
<a id="claim-c07"></a>

- **Draft:** Warfare’s Saar ceiling carries political and tempo costs: early reach can make Saar the table’s shared target and a second-action Warfare can upset neighbors’ planned technology or builds.
  Conditions: Weigh this cost when Saar neighbors can retaliate, when the table dislikes early aggression, or when the proposed movement does not advance scoring. Compatibility: Table-meta advice, not a rules claim. Uncertainty: The level of backlash varies by group; the speakers frame it as common experience.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 3141–3277s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare), [The Clan of Saar](saar.md)
<a id="claim-c08"></a>

- **Draft:** Leadership is a safe, mid-tier Saar pick when command-token momentum will support following Technology, Warfare, or Construction; Saar’s extra carriers create several tempting activations and Fleet Pool can become a ceiling.
  Conditions: Useful when Saar expects multiple activations or needs tokens for round two; avoid spending tokens on low-value movement that leaves the fleet constrained. Compatibility: Guide strategy advice; exact token needs depend on slice and objectives. Uncertainty: Hosts call Leadership solid but not a top priority in every draft.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2520–2625s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Leadership](../components.md#strategy-card-pok1leadership), [Technology](../components.md#strategy-card-pok7technology), [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare), [Construction](../components.md#strategy-card-pok4construction)
<a id="claim-c09"></a>

- **Draft:** Diplomacy supplies money and can enable custodians, but the guide considers it a less attractive round-one custodians route than Saar’s alternatives; Politics can preserve influence for a later Mecatol attempt but delays the point and risks losing the opportunity.
  Conditions: Choose based on slice resources, pick order, and whether an immediate Mecatol point is safer than waiting. Compatibility: Guide opinion about opening cards; current objective landscape not checked. Uncertainty: The hosts debate relative rankings and do not give a single universally best choice.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2629–2750s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Diplomacy](../components.md#strategy-card-pok2diplomacy), [Politics](../components.md#strategy-card-pok3politics), [The Clan of Saar](saar.md)
<a id="claim-c10"></a>

- **Draft:** Trade is a lower-drama way to fund technology, plastic, and possibly custodians while using some of Saar’s Scavenge income to maintain goodwill through deals.
  Conditions: Especially useful when Saar wants money and a less threatening opening than Warfare; trade timing may still depend on Technology or other players’ actions. Compatibility: Guide advice; trade meta varies by group. Uncertainty: Hosts describe Trade as safe and effective but with a lower ceiling than Warfare.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2965–3069s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Trade](../components.md#strategy-card-pok5trade), [Scavenge](../components.md#ability-scavenge), [The Clan of Saar](saar.md)
<a id="claim-c11"></a>

- **Draft:** Keep Saar’s technology plan shallow and prefer plastic when it solves the same movement, economic, or board-presence problem; Chaos Mapping is the guide’s essential technology.
  Conditions: Particularly after early expansion when more ships and ground forces can turn money into objectives; technology objectives or bonuses can change the value calculation. Compatibility: SCPT strategic opinion; no current-rules review. Uncertainty: The guide calls Chaos Mapping essential while describing many other technologies as optional; the exact path remains situational.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 3454–3567s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm), [The Clan of Saar](saar.md)
<a id="claim-c12"></a>

- **Draft:** Research Chaos Mapping early for repeated production. Take Gravity Drive first if it makes round-one custodians or a necessary movement line possible; otherwise Chaos Mapping into Carrier II supports a slower, capacity-focused game without requiring Gravity Drive.
  Conditions: Inspect the slice, custodian race, and floating factory or carrier movement plan before choosing the first technology; Chaos Mapping remains valuable after Gravity Drive. Compatibility: Guide hosts disagree about Gravity Drive’s general value, while agreeing that it is not always required; no ruleset verification. Uncertainty: The source presents competing strategic views and a conditional decision, not a universal technology order.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 3576–3867s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/) · [SCPT 336 3871–3894s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm), [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd), [Carrier II](../components.md#technology-cv2), [Floating Factory I](../components.md#unit-saar-spacedock)
<a id="claim-c13"></a>

- **Draft:** Scavenge grants one trade good after Saar gains a planet, and Saar may then spend one trade good to deploy a mech there; on explored planets, exploration occurs first, so the new reward cannot alter that exploration.
  Conditions: Use the reward for a mech when its board value exceeds retaining the trade good; account for the exploration step before planning the control-trigger reward. Compatibility: Guide timing explanation; current rules not independently checked. Uncertainty: ASR garbles several planet names; claim concerns the named ability sequence only.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 1402–1502s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Scavenge](../components.md#ability-scavenge), [Scavenger Zeta](../components.md#unit-saar-mech)
<a id="claim-c14"></a>

- **Draft:** Chaos Mapping lets Saar produce one unit at the start of each of its turns in a system with one of its units that has Production; this is distinct from using the Production ability, so the guide says Sarween Tools does not apply to this effect.
  Conditions: Research early to gain more triggers; select units and systems that support future actions without assuming this replaces a normal production build or creates a stall. Compatibility: SCPT’s rule interpretation, including a wording distinction; validate against current rules if exact legality is required. Uncertainty: The episode notes production terminology is confusing; this summary preserves the guide’s asserted distinction.
  Sources: [SCPT 336 2076–2156s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/) · [SCPT 336 2223–2286s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/336-super-clan-of-saar-guide/)
  Components: [Chaos Mapping](../components.md#technology-cm), [Sarween Tools](../components.md#technology-st)
<a id="claim-c15"></a>

- **Draft:** An infantry-first opening can secure planets without tying up ship capacity; later pivot into fighters once Carrier II and the board position make a stronger space screen useful.
  Conditions: Best when early opponents lack enough infantry to contest Saar’s planets and Saar can still protect critical fleets; do not leave key systems exposed. Compatibility: A strategy tip attributed in the guide to experienced Saar player Empson; not a universal rule. Uncertainty: The source provides one example of a successful large infantry footprint; outcomes depend on diplomacy and opponents.

<a id="claim-c16"></a>

- **Draft:** Once Saar has enough technology for its plan, compare each optional technology with the ships or fighters the same resources could buy; the guide usually favors plastic that advances board presence or scoring.
  Conditions: Applies when Saar has a viable production opportunity and no revealed technology objective or bonus makes the technology especially valuable. Compatibility: Guide strategic heuristic; unit costs and resource availability vary by game state. Uncertainty: The hosts frame the comparison as a rule of thumb rather than an exact calculation.

<a id="claim-c17"></a>

- **Draft:** Floating Factory II can improve movement and production when Saar can afford the yellow route without delaying urgent needs; commander routing still respects production capacity and cannot place units at a blockaded destination dock.
  Conditions: Consider the upgrade in technology-rich games or with helpful yellow access; assess actual build money and whether remote production sites are unblocked. Compatibility: Guide description of Saar unit upgrade and commander; present rules not verified. Uncertainty: ASR has a clipped line about production/capacity values; the summary avoids relying on its exact numerical detail.

<a id="claim-c18"></a>

- **Draft:** Captain Mendosa can raise an activated ship’s move value to the highest move value on the board; Saar’s starting cruiser supports a round-one move-two carrier or factory, and Gravity Drive can add movement afterward.
  Conditions: Use when a specific reach breakpoint matters, such as a custodians attempt; selling the agent may be reasonable if Saar does not expect to reach custodians and a buyer offers value. Compatibility: Guide interpretation of the Saar agent; current movement rules not independently checked. Uncertainty: The transcript discusses modifiers and terrain as caveats; this is not a promise of a clear route or a fixed total movement.

<a id="claim-c19"></a>

- **Draft:** Chaos Mapping protects Saar ships in asteroid fields from opponents activating those systems, but non-activation effects such as the guide’s Benediction example can still move ships out and expose Saar.
  Conditions: Treat asteroid positions as temporary protection and keep alternate survival or retreat paths, especially before passing or when an opponent has a relevant movement effect. Compatibility: Guide’s POK-era interaction discussion; not independently rules-checked. Uncertainty: The exact referenced card/ability wording may be ASR-imperfect; transcript clearly warns that protection is not absolute.

- **Draft:** Do not assume Saar is safe merely because it can score without home planets or shelter ships in asteroid fields; overextension and a moment outside protection can let the table coordinate an elimination attempt.

Compatibility: Guide strategic warning; elimination and timing rules not separately reviewed. Uncertainty: The guide describes table behavior and threat windows from play experience.
